intent: A non-modal inspector dialog, docked beside the inspector rail, holding an auto-layout frame's three secondary settings: stroke inclusion, canvas stacking, and text-baseline alignment.
guidance: Open it from the auto-layout section's settings trigger; it renders through InspectorDialog, so it docks to the inspector surface's left edge with an 8px gutter (not to the trigger) and lands clear of the panel wherever the trigger sits (#661). Non-modal: the canvas stays live, focus is not trapped, and Escape, the close X, or an outside click all call onClose. Fully controlled — emit committed patches via onChange and re-render with the new value; the dialog keeps no state. In grid mode only the Strokes row renders. Off the horizontal axis the text-baseline toggle is disabled and explains itself through a tooltip — keep it visible rather than hiding it.

anatomy.description: The portalled non-modal floating panel from InspectorDialog: 240px wide (COMPACT_INSPECTOR_DIALOG_WIDTH), rounded-c-lg, bg-c-bg, elevation/400, docked the 8px gutter clear of the inspector surface's left edge; draggable and edge-aware.
The 40px title bar (border-b border-c-border, px-[12px]); the dialog's first child, so it doubles as the drag handle.
The "Auto layout settings" h2 in type/body-medium-strong, color/text.
24px button, aria-label "Close Auto layout settings", 16px X glyph in icon/secondary; rounded-c-sm with a c-focus-ring focus ring. Calls onClose.
A 104px label column (type/body-medium, color/text-secondary) beside a full-width control; min-height 32px.
Full-width Dropdown opening a radio menu — Excluded / Included; shows "Mixed" for multi-selection.
Full-width Dropdown opening a radio menu — First on top / Last on top; shows "Mixed" for multi-selection. Hidden in grid mode.
Two-segment SegmentedControl (Minus = off, Check = on); disabled with a tooltip "Only applicable for horizontal layouts" off the horizontal axis. Hidden in grid mode.

use_when: Editing an auto-layout frame's stroke inclusion, canvas stacking, or text-baseline alignment — the secondary settings that don't earn a permanent inspector row.
You need a small surface docked beside the inspector that leaves the canvas interactive while it's open.
dont_use_when: A blocking task or confirmation — use Modal.
The primary auto-layout controls (direction, gap, padding, alignment) — those live inline in the inspector section, not here.
A free-standing option list with no dialog chrome — use Menu / Dropdown.

slots.trigger: The launch control (a ReactElement) the dialog anchors to and captures; focus returns here on close.

tokens.note: No #hex color in source — every color binds to a c-* token. Spacing is hardcoded px (header 40, body inset 12, row gap 4, row min-height 32, label column 104, control gap 8); the 240px width, 8px surface-anchored gutter and elevation 400 come from shared InspectorDialog constants (COMPACT_INSPECTOR_DIALOG_WIDTH, AUTO_LAYOUT_SETTINGS_INSPECTOR_SIDE_OFFSET, COMPOSA_INSPECTOR_SURFACE_SELECTOR).

a11y.role: dialog — non-modal (aria-modal=false, no focus trap). The role is rendered by the InspectorDialog overlay surface, not literally in this component's source, so ariaRole is not enforced here.
a11y.label: aria-label "Auto layout settings" names the dialog (there is no title-element association).
a11y.close: The header X is a <button aria-label="Close Auto layout settings">; Escape and outside-click also call onClose.
a11y.controls: Each Dropdown carries a descriptive aria-label (e.g. "Stroke inclusion: Excluded") and opens menuitemradio rows; the text-baseline SegmentedControl is a role="group" of aria-pressed segments, and its disabled state is explained via a tooltip.
a11y.focus: Non-modal — focus is not trapped; the canvas stays interactive and focus returns to the trigger on close.

code.example:
<AutoLayoutSettingsDialog
  open={open}
  value={{ mode: 'horizontal', textBaseline: false, strokeSizing: 'excluded', canvasStacking: 'last-on-top' }}
  trigger={<IconButton icon={<Settings2 />} ariaLabel="Auto layout settings" />}
  onChange={patch => commit(patch)}
  onClose={() => setOpen(false)}
/>
